_comment: The REAL AIIMS Delhi 2022 incident, as established by official Government of India parliamentary answers. This exists to sit beside our SYNTHETIC aiims_ransomware scenario and show the difference between what is established and what everyone assumes. Every quote below was extracted from the primary-source PDF, not copied from secondary reporting. Facts nobody has published stay in not_established, where they belong.
title: AIIMS Delhi ransomware incident, November 2022
verification_method: Primary-source PDFs fetched from sansad.in and text-extracted; quotes below are verbatim from those documents.

sources.ministry: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
sources.answered_by: Shri Rajeev Chandrasekhar, Minister of State
sources.subject: CYBER SECURITY ATTACKS
sources.note: Text extracted directly from the fetched PDF on 2026-08-19.

sources.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
sources.answered_by: Dr. Bharati Pravin Pawar, Minister of State
sources.subject: CYBER-ATTACK IN AIIMS
sources.note: Text extracted directly from the fetched PDF on 2026-08-19.

sources.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
sources.note: Cited in our research but NOT re-verified here: the host returned HTTP 403 when fetched on 2026-08-19. Nothing in this case file depends on it.

established_facts.fact: Five AIIMS Delhi servers were affected and approximately 1.3 TB of data was encrypted.
established_facts.quote: Based on current analysis by concerned stakeholders, five servers of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi were affected and approximately 1.3 Tera Bytes of data was encrypted.

established_facts.fact: Servers in the AIIMS IT network were compromised by unknown threat actors, and improper network segmentation contributed to operational disruption.
established_facts.quote: As per the analysis, servers in the information technology network of AIIMS were compromised by unknown threat actors due to improper network segmentation, which caused operational disruption due to non-functionality of critical applications.

established_facts.fact: The five affected physical servers hosted the NIC e-Hospital application.
established_facts.quote: Five physical servers of AIIMS, New Delhi on which e-Hospital application of NIC was hosted, were affected.

established_facts.fact: No specific ransom amount was demanded; a message on the server suggested a cyber-attack.
established_facts.quote: No specific amount of ransom was demanded by the hackers though a message was discovered on the server suggesting that it was a cyber- attack.

established_facts.fact: Data was recovered from an unaffected backup server and restored onto new servers.
established_facts.quote: All the data for e-Hospital has been retrieved from a backup server which was unaffected and restored on new servers.

established_facts.fact: Most e-Hospital functions were restored about two weeks after the attack.
established_facts.quote: Most of the functions of e-Hospital application like patient registration, appointment, admission, discharge etc. have been restored after two weeks of the cyber-attack.

established_facts.fact: An FIR was registered with the Special Cell of Delhi Police.
established_facts.quote: A First Information Report (FIR) No. 349/22 has been registered by the All India Institute of Medical Sciences with the Special Cell of Delhi Police under relevant sections of law, regarding the incident of cyber-attack.

attack_claims.rationale: The Government explicitly reported that approximately 1.3 TB of data was encrypted and that critical applications became non-functional. Encryption plus availability disruption is exactly what T1486 describes.

Five servers were affected rather than one, which makes lateral movement a reasonable investigation hypothesis. No public source establishes it, and it must not be shown as observed without forensic evidence.
missing_evidence: authentication and session logs between the affected servers
endpoint or EDR telemetry from the compromised hosts
the forensic timeline held by CERT-In and the investigating agency
alternatives: five servers independently exposed through the same weakness
a shared administrative credential or deployment channel used to reach all five without host-to-host movement
a common vulnerable service reachable from the same flat network segment

control_weaknesses.quote: compromised by unknown threat actors due to improper network segmentation
control_weaknesses.note: A control weakness, NOT an ATT&CK technique. It belongs in the defensive model, not the adversary model.

not_established: the specific remote service or lateral-movement technique, if any
whether data was exfiltrated as well as encrypted
the identity or nationality of the threat actors
why_this_matters: A complete-looking kill chain for this incident would be fabricated. The Government established one technique. Everything else that circulates about AIIMS 2022 — the initial vector, the family, the actor, the data theft — is not in the public record. This case file exists so the product demonstrates that distinction instead of quietly filling the gaps.

relationship_to_scenario.note: The shipped aiims_ransomware scenario is SYNTHETIC. It is styled after this incident to give a realistic Indian critical-infrastructure story with named crown jewels, but its hosts, accounts and events are generated. It is not a reconstruction of the real attack and must never be presented as one.
